text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- TRADE DEFICIT HITS $2 BLN IN THE FIRST TWO MONTHS
Brazil posted a $2.031 billion trade deficit in the January-to-February period. Imports totalled $8.862 billion, while exports amounted to $6.831 billion in the first two months.
-- LOWER HOUSE COMMITTEE APPROVES OIL BILL
The government succeeded in having approved in a lower house committee a bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's oil and gas industries.
Twenty-three members of the committee approved the bill presented by Deputy Eliseu Resende without alterations.

Two international rating agencies, Duff & Phelps and Standard & Poors, are reviewing their rating for Brazil. Duff & Phelps is likely to maintain its BB- rating for the country, while Standard & Poors may upgrade its rating.
Results of an exam taken by college students aimed at testing the quality of Brazilian universities showed a disappointing situation at the country's universities.
-- PC FARIAS AND DRUG DEALER HAD ACCOUNT IN SWITZERLAND
Paulo Cesar Farias, ex-treasurer of former President Fernando Collor, and the chief of a drug trafficking network linked to the Italian Mafia had an account together in a Swiss bank.
-- RIO'S CITY COUNCIL PROPOSAL RAISES PROPERTY TAX BY 20 PCT
Rio de Janeiro mayor Luiz Paulo Conde on Tuesday presented a bill that would raise by 20 percent on average the city's property tax.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
